title: An immersion has fibres of degree at most one (Stacks 03J9)
statement: Let $j:Z\to X$ be an immersion of schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion] (a closed immersion followed by an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]). Then the integer $1$ bounds the degrees of the fibres of $j$ [def-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-bound]: for every $x\in X$ the fibre $Z_x=Z\times_X\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$ is finite over $\kappa(x)$ with $\dim_{\kappa(x)}\Gamma(Z_x,\mathcal O_{Z_x})\le1$ (it is empty if $x\notin j(Z)$ and isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$ over $\kappa(x)$ if $x\in j(Z)$). In particular the fibres of $j$ are universally bounded. (Stacks Project, Morphisms, Lemma Tag 03J9.)

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tag 03J9 (lemma-immersion-universally-bounded), line 15459, and its proof ('The integer n = 1 works')

proof.text: *The fibre is an immersion into the spectrum of a field.* Let $x\in X$, let $c_x:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$ be the canonical morphism, and let $Z_x=Z\times_X\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$ be the fibre of $j$ at $x$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre], a fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] with projections $p:Z_x\to Z$ and $q:Z_x\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$. The morphism $q$ is the projection $Z\times_X\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$ of the base change of the immersion $j$ along $c_x$, hence an immersion [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft] (1) (Stacks Schemes 01JY): $q=o\circ c$ with $c:Z_x\to U$ a closed immersion and $o:U\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$ an open immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion].

source.place: Schemes, Lemma Tag 01JY (lemma-base-change-immersion), used for the fibre in the proof of Morphisms Lemma 03J9

proof.text: *The open part.* The field $\kappa=\kappa(x)$ has exactly one prime ideal, $(0)$, so $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] has exactly one point, and its only open subsets are $\emptyset$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa$. The open immersion $o$ is a homeomorphism of $U$ onto an open subset of $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa$ [def-weil-open-immersion]. If that subset is $\emptyset$, then $U=\emptyset$, hence $Z_x=\emptyset$ since $c$ maps $Z_x$ into $U$. Otherwise it is all of $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa$, and $o$ is an isomorphism of $U$ with the open subscheme $(\operatorname{Spec}\kappa,\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa})$, i.e. $o$ is an isomorphism of schemes [def-weil-open-immersion].

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma Tag 03J9 (lemma-immersion-universally-bounded), line 15459 ('The integer n = 1 works in the definition'); the steps the source leaves out written out

proof.text: *The closed part.* Suppose $o$ is an isomorphism. Then $q=o\circ c$ is a closed immersion: composing with the isomorphism $o$ keeps $q$ a homeomorphism onto a closed subset and keeps $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa}\to q_*\mathcal O_{Z_x}$ surjective (it is the surjection $\mathcal O_U\to c_*\mathcal O_{Z_x}$ transported along $o$) [def-weil-closed-immersion]. By the affine form of the definition [def-weil-closed-immersion] (Stacks 01QO) applied to the affine open $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa$ itself, there is an ideal $I\subseteq\kappa$ with $Z_x\cong\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa/I)$ over $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. As $\kappa$ is a field, $I=\kappa$ or $I=0$. If $I=\kappa$, then $\kappa/I=0$ has no prime ideal and $Z_x=\emptyset$. If $I=0$, then $q$ is the composite of an isomorphism $Z_x\cong\operatorname{Spec}\kappa$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(\mathrm{id}_\kappa)$, so $q$ is an isomorphism. Together with step 2: either $Z_x=\emptyset$ or $q:Z_x\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma Tag 03J9 (lemma-immersion-universally-bounded), line 15459 ('The integer n = 1 works in the definition'); the steps the source leaves out written out

proof.text: *Which case occurs.* The first projection $p$ is a homeomorphism of $Z_x$ onto $j^{-1}(x)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. So $Z_x=\emptyset$ exactly when $j^{-1}(x)=\emptyset$, i.e. when $x\notin j(Z)$; by step 3, for $x\in j(Z)$ the morphism $q$ is an isomorphism $Z_x\cong\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$ over $\kappa(x)$.

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma Tag 03J9 (lemma-immersion-universally-bounded), line 15459 ('The integer n = 1 works in the definition'); the steps the source leaves out written out

proof.text: *Degree at most one.* If $Z_x=\emptyset$: the inverse image under $q$ of any affine open of $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$ is $\emptyset=\operatorname{Spec}(0)$, which is affine, so $q$ is affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism], and the ring maps $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O)\to0$ are finite, so $q$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], with $\dim_{\kappa(x)}\Gamma(Z_x,\mathcal O_{Z_x})=\dim 0=0$. If $q$ is an isomorphism: the inverse image of an affine open $V$ is isomorphic to $V$ through $q$, hence affine, and the ring map $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O)\to\Gamma(q^{-1}V,\mathcal O)$ is an isomorphism, hence finite, so $q$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and $\Gamma(Z_x,\mathcal O_{Z_x})\cong\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x),\mathcal O)=\kappa(x)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] as $\kappa(x)$-algebras, of dimension $1$. In both cases $Z_x$ is finite over $\kappa(x)$ of degree $\le1$; as $x$ was arbitrary, $1$ bounds the degrees of the fibres of $j$ and the fibres of $j$ are universally bounded [def-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-bound].

Proof written out in 5 steps: the fibre's projection q: Z_x -> Spec kappa(x) is a base change of j, hence an immersion o∘c (lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft (1), Stacks 01JY); the open part o is empty or an isomorphism since Spec of a field is one point (definition of open immersion); the closed part into Spec kappa is Spec(kappa/I) with I=0 or kappa (affine form of def-weil-closed-immersion, Stacks 01QO); the fibre is empty iff x not in j(Z) (def-pc-scheme-fibre); degree 0 or 1 and finiteness checked from def-weil-finite-integral-morphism.
